Nidhi Gupta, J.

Present appeal has been filed by the injured-claimant claimant seeking enhancement of compensation of Rs.
Rs.9,46,095/- awarded by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Panchkula (hereinafter referred to as "the Tribunal"), vide Award dated 04.09.2017 passed in MACP Case No.215/2015 dated 30.11.2015 filed led under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act (hereinafter referred to as "the Act").
2. Brief facts of the case are that the ld. Tribunal on the basis of pleadings and oral & documentary evidence adduced before it concluded that the appellant/injured-claimant appellant/injured claimant had suffered injuries in a motor vehicular accident that took place on 21.01.2015 due to the rash and negligent driving of truck bearing registration No. No.HP-64-2452 (hereinafter referred to as "the offending vehicle") by respondent No.1.
The offending 1 of 6 Neutral Citation No:=2025:PHHC:057538 vehicle was owned by respondent No.2 and insured by respondent No.3.

sentences.text: The above-said said compensation was granted along with interest @ 6% % per annum.

3. Learned counsel for or the appellant appellant/injured-claimant claimant seeks enhancement of compensation by submitting that income of the appellant has been taken on the lower side as Rs.9,800/ Rs.9,800/- per month only;;
whereas it was the clearly pleaded case of the appellant that he was a driver by profession rofession and was getting a salary of Rs.10,000/ Rs.10,000/- per month..

It is submitted that the occupation and income of the appellant was duly proved from the evidence of PW4 Gurnam Singh who had submitted his affidavit (Ex.PW4/A) and had deposed that he is owner o off tractor bearing registration No.HR-49C-4141;
No.HR 4141; and that the appellant was employed with him as a driver and that he was paying a salary of Rs.10,000/ Rs.10,000/- per month to the appellant.
It is submitted that therefore income of the appellant ought to have been taken tak as 10,000/- per month instead of 9800/- per month.
4. It is further submitted that the appellant has suffered 45% permanent disability.

However,
nothing has been granted to the appellant on account of pain & suffering and mental agony.

In fact,
the learned Tribunal is in error in taking permanent disability of the appellant as only 33%
functional disability; whereas functional disability also ought to have been taken as 45%.
It is accordingly prayed that the impugned Award be modified.

5. Learned counsel for the respondent No.3/Insurance Company opposes the prayer made on behalf of the appellant and submits that it is a clear finding of the learned Tribunal that the occupation and employment or even the salary of the appellant were not proved on record.
It is further pointed out that the appellant has failed to prove his disability before the learned Tribunal.
Learned counsel accordingly prays for dismissal of the present appeal.
6. No other argument is made on behalf of the parties.
2 of 6 Neutral Citation No:=2025:PHHC:057538 7.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused d the case file in great detail.

8. Perusal of record of the case shows that it was the pleaded case of the appellant in the claim petition that on 21.01.2015, the claimant being pillion rider on motorcycle bearing registration No.
HR HR-49-C-- 0264 which was being driven by Randhir Singh, was going from Nalagarh, district Solan (HP) to his house at village Nawa Nagar, tehsil Kalka, district Panchkula.
The motorcycle was being driven by Randhir Singh on correct left side of the road.

At about 07.00 PM, when they reached on Manpura main road on Baddi-Nalagarh Baddi Nalagarh road, a truck vehicle bearing registration No.HP-64-2452 2452 (for short 'offending vehicle') being dr driven iven by the respondent Gurdhyan Singh vs Garib Dass And Ors on 2 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69089550/
2 no.1-Garib no.1 Garib Dass rashly and negligently, came from Baddi side and hit against the motorcycle.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As a result of accident, the claimant and aforesaid Randhir Singh fell down on the road and both of them suffered severe and grievous injuries injuries on their respective persons.
After causing the accident, the respondent no.1 stopped for short time, but thereafter, he along with the offending vehicle sped away from the spot.

The claimant being injured was taken to FRU Hospital,
Nalagarh, from where he was referred to PGI, Chandigarh.
He also took treatment from Akash Hospital, Nalagarh and Max City Hospital, Ropar (Punjab).
In PGI and Max City Hospital, Ropar he was operated upon and steel rod, screws etc. were inserted in his fractured bones of thigh.
thigh.
He had spent an amount of Rs. 8 lakhs on this treatment.

On the basis of statement made by an eyewitness Gurbachan Singh, FIR No.11 dated 21.01.2015 under sections 279, 338 of IPC was registered against the respondent no.1, being driver of the offending vehicle, at police station Baddi.

As per the claimant, at the time of occurrence of the accident in question, question, he was working as driver and was also doing dairy farming and had monthly income to the tune of Rs.20,000/- from both the avocations.
Claimant prayed that he is entitled to compensation in the sum of Rs.30 lakhs along with interest.

3 of 6 Neutral Citation No:=2025:PHHC:057538 9. However, at the he time of argument, it has only been contended by the appellant that he was employed as a driver and was drawing a salary of Rs.10,000/-
Rs.10,000/ per month.

In support, the appellant had produced his Driving Licence (Ex.PX) as per which he was authorised to drive motorcycle with gear, light motor vehicle i.e. non non-transport transport car, light motor vehicle and tractor.

To o prove his employment as a driver, the appellant had produced PW4 Gurnam Singh, who had submitted his affidavit deposing that the appellant was employed with him and used to drive his tractor bearing registration No.HR No.HR-49C-4141, 4141,
registration certificate of which was placed on record as Ex.P66.
However, Gurnam Singh did id not produce any documentary evidence to prove the said employment of the appellant.

Even no document was brought on record to prove that the appellant was drawing a salary of Rs.10,000/
Rs.10,000/- per month..
There is also nothing on record to show that appellant was doing the work of dairy farming.

Thus,
learned Tribunal had d taken income of the appellant as Rs.9,800/-
Rs.9,800/ per month on the basis of Notification dated 05.06.2014 issued by the Deputy Commissioner, Panchkula for the relevant Financial Year 2014-15 15,, as per which the driver authorised to drive light motor vehicles, was getting monthly salary of Rs.9,800/ Rs.9,800/-.
As such, income of the appellant was correctly assessed.

10. It has next been contended by the appellant that in the accident in question, he had had suffered 45% permanent disability, which has been wrongly taken as only on y 33% functional disability by the learned Tribunal.

To prove the same, the appellant had examined Dr. K.K. Bansal PW2,, who deposed that: "... the claimant was an operated case of compound fracture SOF right with fracture Gurdhyan Singh vs Garib Dass And Ors on 2 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69089550/
3 acetabulum right with Nail right thigh and restriction of movements at right hip and right knee with loss of thigh muscle mess...".
PW2 also proved Disability Certificate ((Ex.P63) of the appellant.
However, admittedly, PW2 was not the treating doctor of the appellant..

Thus, in actual fact, the appellant had failed to prove his 4 of 6 Neutral Citation No:=2025:PHHC:057538 disability/disability certificate as he had failed to examine the doctor whose treatment he had undergone.

However,, the learned Tribunal placed reliance upon judgment of Andhra Pradesh High Court in "Sannala Bhaskar Reddy Vs. M. Sreenivasulu & Another" Law Finder doc ID # 215848 and took disability of the appellant to be 33% functional disability disability.

entities.text: Sannala Bhaskar Reddy Vs. M. Sreenivasulu & Another" Law Finder doc ID # 215848
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said case also, the disability certificate was not proved as the treating doctor was not examined.
Yet, the Andhra Pradesh High Court had assessed the disability of the injured therein to be 25%.

11. Accordingly, the learned Tribunal had taken monthly loss of income of the appellant to be Rs.3,234/-
Rs.3,234/- (33% of Rs.9,800/-)..

As age of the appellant was taken to be 19 years as per the record,
accordingly multiplier of 18 was correctly applied and compensatio compensationn amount was determined to be Rs.6,98,544/-
Rs.6,98,544/ (Rs.3,234/-- x 12 x 18)..

The appellant had further produced bills Ex.P1 to Ex.P24,
Ex.P24, Ex.P26 to Ex.P30, Ex.P32 to Ex.p56 and Ex.P60,, for an amount of Rs.2,25,551/-,
Rs.2,25,551/ , which was duly granted to the appellant.
The appellant appellant was further shown to have remained hospitalised for 23 days.

Learned Tribunal accordingly, awarded Rs.23,000/
Rs.23,000/- towards hospitalisation, special diet, transportation; thus, granting total compensation of Rs.9,46,095/-
Rs.9,46,095/ (Rs.6,98,544/ (Rs.6,98,544/- + Rs.2,25,551/- + Rs.23,000/-- ).
12.
From the above facts, it is clear that no case is made out which merits interference with the impugned Award.
No doubt Chapter-12 12 of the Act is a beneficial legislation yet, as cautioned by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, the same cannot be allowed to be treated as a windfall or a source of profit.

Hon'ble Supreme Court in ''State of Haryana & Another Vs. Jasbir Kaur & Others' Law Finder Doc ID # 64043 and 'Divisional Controller K.S.R.T.C. Vs. Mahadev Shetty', (2003) 7 SCC 197, has held that the the amount of compensation should be just and reasonable, it should neither be a bonanza nor a source of profit but at the same time it should not be a pittance.

sentences.text:
In the present case,
am more than just 5 of 6 Neutral Citation No:=2025:PHHC:057538 compensation has been awarded to the appellant.

In the case of "General Manager, KSRTC Vs. Susamma Thomas & Others"
1994 Volume Volume-II SCC 176, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that misplaced sympathy,
generosity and benevolence cannot be the guiding factor for determining the compensation.
